bugatti-assembly-229431.text:
制作一套具有顶级汽车发布片质感的 Blender 产品动画。主角是蓝绿/青蓝色 Bugatti Tourbillon：低矮宽体、精确轮廓、清晰的分件装配和奢华的机械式座舱。三个短片分别让观众看清车辆怎样组成、完整外观有多精致、座舱的机械仪表为什么迷人。

完成场景、材质、绑定与动画，最终导出 3 段代表性视频、6 张高质量宣传图，并保存可编辑的 Blender 工程。

场景与动作

• 车身是中置座舱、低矮宽体的双座超跑，前后轮拱饱满，座舱呈紧凑泪滴形，车头低且宽，尾部收束锐利。建议以长约 4.7 米、宽约 2 米、高约 1.2 米的视觉尺度搭建，轴距约占车长六成、轮胎外径略大于车高一半，以此协调车身的整体比例。正中为立起的黑色马蹄形格栅，左右是极细分段灯组；两侧大进气口、向后上挑的肩线、深色碳纤维车顶与青蓝车壳形成分区。青蓝车漆具有底色、金属细闪和清漆层，反射沿前翼子板、肩线和后轮拱的曲面连续移动。
• 模块至少覆盖底盘、四轮/轮毂/刹车、前后车身、座舱、玻璃和两扇门。需要在爆炸视图中出现的零件具有独立厚度和合理背面，门缝、进气开口和接合边缘具有真实深度，可见内构采用可信的机械展示结构。
• 两扇门以 A 柱附近为旋转支点，向上且向外作斜向展开，门打开时露出座椅和低门槛，保持铰链净空。座舱包括奶油色与黑色双座、带缝线的软包、金属饰条、中控与方向盘；多层模拟机械仪表盘具有真正的环圈、指针、玻璃盖与刻度层级，近景能看清各层之间的深度与细小高光。
• 展厅为暗色空间、竖向灯带、具有适度反射的深色地面与环形发光展台。大面积柔光塑造车身，细长灯条在漆面上形成可控高光；轮胎、碳纤维、金属、皮革与玻璃的响应各不相同。

组装采用展览式受控悬浮，部件按次序对齐、靠近、落位，运动路径留出足够净空。透明车窗透出座舱的层次，整支短片突出 Bugatti Tourbillon 的车身曲线与机械式座舱。

london-sky-diorama-930161.text:
Create a single self-contained HTML file using three.js that renders an ultra-detailed voxel diorama of LONDON on a floating island in the sky. Super high detail, cinematic quality, saturated colors.
ISLAND
Irregular oval floating island (not a perfect circle), wavy organic coastline.
Thick cliff sides with layered rock strata (orange, tan, brown, grey bands), mossy rock outcrops, hanging roots, green vines with small flowers dripping off the rim.
Jagged underside tapering into stalactite-like rock spikes.
The Thames runs across the whole island in turquoise-blue water with light waves, and pours off both edges as waterfalls with mist at the bottom. Add 3–4 smaller waterfalls off the rim.
6 small floating islets around it, each with a tiny prop: a red phone box, a street lamp, a pond, a cottage with a red roof, a flower bed. One islet has its own mini waterfall.

LANDMARKS (instantly recognizable, the main focus; no generic houses or apartment blocks)
Palace of Westminster with gothic spires along the roof, Victoria Tower with a waving Union Jack, and Big Ben (Elizabeth Tower) with 4 working clock faces and moving hands.
London Eye: big white wheel with glass pods, slowly rotating.
Tower Bridge: two stone towers, blue walkways, bascules slowly lifting and lowering.
The Shard (glossy glass pyramid) and the Gherkin (glossy glass bullet with diagonal stripes) on the skyline.
St Paul's Cathedral with a dome; Tower of London (White Tower with 4 turrets and curtain walls).
Buckingham Palace with the golden Victoria Memorial in front, ringed by red flower beds; Queen's Guards in red tunics and black bearskins marching.
Trafalgar Square: Nelson's Column, 4 lions, 2 fountains, the National Gallery behind.
Westminster Bridge with lamps.

PARKS & LIFE
Everything else is lush parkland: striped lawns, winding gravel paths, varied trees (big round plane trees, slim poplars, pink blossom trees), colorful flower beds, lamp posts and red phone boxes along the embankments.
Hundreds of tiny walking people, red double-decker buses and black cabs driving, river boats on the Thames, seagulls flying.
3 hot-air balloons in Union Jack colors drifting around the island; small white voxel clouds.

LIGHTING & RENDER
Sunny late morning: warm low sun with long soft shadows, deep blue gradient sky, bright saturated colors, subtle bloom, ACES tone mapping, ambient occlusion, high-quality antialiasing.

CAMERA & ANIMATION
12-second loop at 30 fps, with motion from the very first frame.
Smooth slow orbit around the island (about 50°) with a very light zoom-in. No close-ups, the whole island always in frame.
Everything animated: wheel turning, bridge lifting, clock hands, buses, boats, people, waterfalls, balloons, islets gently bobbing.

liberty-island-1886-433422.text:
Build a single self-contained HTML file (three.js r160 from cdn.jsdelivr via importmap) that renders a detailed voxel diorama: "Liberty Island & New York, autumn 1886 — dedication day of the Statue of Liberty", as a floating island in a warm hazy sky.

STYLE
- Chunky voxels with slightly beveled (chamfered) edges, vertex colors with per-voxel color jitter and baked ambient occlusion.
- Golden-hour light: low warm sun (ACES tone mapping, soft PCF shadows), sky-dome gradient with a sun glow, warm haze fog, subtle bloom.
- Floating island: grassy rim, layered rock strata on the sides, a jagged rocky underside with hanging stalactites. Small floating islets with autumn trees drift around it, plus a few voxel clouds.

LAYOUT
- Center: Bedloe's Island with star-shaped Fort Wood (11 points, granite + red brick walls), autumn trees, a seawall, small piers.
- On it: the granite pedestal with its loggia openings, and THE STATUE (must be instantly recognizable): green patina, flowing robe with vertical folds and a diagonal sash, raised right arm holding a torch with a balcony and a glowing gold flame, a tablet in the left arm with "JULY IV MDCCLXXVI", a crown with 7 rays and windows, a broad face.
- Around it: a harbor ring of animated water with waves, a paddle-wheel ferry, a tugboat with smoke, and a three-masted sailing ship.
- Behind it: a crescent of 1886 Manhattan on a street grid. Brownstones, red-brick tenements with black iron fire escapes, cast-iron store buildings with striped awnings, waterfront warehouses, wooden water tanks on the rooftops, chimneys with smoke, gas lamps with warm glow, a few lit windows, a gothic Trinity-style church with a tall spire, a white New England steeple church, a Central-Park-style green with a pond and a bandstand, US flags on rooftops.
- A river channel cuts through the city to the island edge, with the Brooklyn Bridge over it: granite towers with twin gothic arches, 4 main cables, vertical suspenders and the diagonal stay web, carriages and pedestrians crossing.
- An elevated railway (the El) on iron columns along one avenue, with a small steam engine pulling 3 cars and puffing smoke.
- Waterfalls pour off the island rim where the water reaches the edge, with mist at the bottom.

LIFE (all deterministic, driven by time t)
- Hundreds of tiny voxel people: pedestrians on sidewalks, crowds on the waterfront and a dedication grandstand with red-white-blue bunting, some waving and some holding parasols.
- Horse-drawn cabs on the streets, waving flags, seagulls circling the statue, smoke and steam particles.

CAMERA & OUTPUT
- A 10-second slow orbit of about 100° around the whole island with a slight zoom-in, the island always fully in frame (like a turntable showcase shot).
- Expose window.renderAt(t) for frame-by-frame capture at 30 or 60 fps, canvas sized from URL params ?w=&h= (default 1920x1080).
- Performance: merge static voxels into chunked meshes, cull hidden faces, use instancing for people and particles, and render the static shadow map once.

mount-fuji-comparison-505326.text:
Build a photoreal, real-time Mount Fuji as a static, no-build-step three.js r169 page (ES modules + import map, three.js vendored locally) served by a tiny http://serve.py on port 9013 (no-cache headers, threaded, listen backlog 256 because the page loads ~40 modules at once). Every asset is generated in code: no downloaded models, image files, HDRIs or AI textures. Textures are painted on 2D canvases at load or computed in shaders. Heavy precomputation runs in Web Workers behind a minimal loading bar and is cached in IndexedDB so the second load opens in about a second.

The goal: someone who knows Fuji recognises the exact mountain, not a generic volcano. Real geography, real scale, real sun. Real place names are fine; no rail operator, airline or brand names or logos.

1. World frame
Metres, y up, origin at the summit's ground position, sea level y = 0, +x east, -z north.
80 x 80 km world (Fuji Five Lakes, Misaka range, Suruga Bay all inside). Far plane 120 km.
Logarithmic depth buffer. Every custom ShaderMaterial includes the logdepthbuf chunks. For the terrain, write log depth in the vertex stage instead (gl_Position.z = (log2(max(1e-6, 1.0 + w)) * logDepthBufFC - 1.0) * w) so early-Z still culls hidden ridges; three's per-fragment log depth disables it and costs 15-47 % of frame time.
Earth curvature in every vertex shader: y -= |dxz|^2 * uCurv.
Real sun and moon: NOAA solar position for 35.36 N, 138.73 E from a JST date and time.
2. The mountain
Float32 heightfields in a worker: 4096 x 4096 over 80 km plus 2048 x 2048 over the central 16 x 16 km cone, blended with smoothstep(80, 500, distance to cone edge). Mip chains for both. The same data feeds the GPU (float textures) and a JS sampler that matches the GPU bilinear exactly (used for raycasts, camera clamping and object placement).
Concave-up radial profile, relative to a ~850 m base: coneRel(r_km) = 2615.14 * exp(-(r / 6.3762)^1.231) + 591.92 * exp(-r / 1.0659), giving ~3,776 m at the rim, ~3,000 m at 2 km, ~2,300 m at 4 km, ~1,500 m at 8 km, ~1,000 m at 14 km. 8 % stretch on the NW-SE axis; the north apron stays higher than the south.
Ouchi-in crater: ~700 m across, ~230 m deep, eight rim peaks, Kengamine highest on the SW rim. From afar the top must read flat and slightly notched, never rounded.
Hoei crater on the SE flank (~1.3 km, rim ~2,700 m, open downslope) with the Hoei-zan hump below it: a bulge on the right skyline from the south, on the left from Gotemba, hidden from Lake Kawaguchi.
Osawa-kuzure on the WSW flank down to ~2,200 m, up to 500 m wide and 150 m deep, jagged red-brown headwall.
Radial gullies from ridged noise in polar coordinates at periodic angular levels (30 / 60 / 120 / 240 per turn, increasing with radius), then a 300,000-droplet hydraulic erosion pass with deposition; smooth lava aprons below ~2,000 m. ~60 flank cones mostly on the NW-SE axis, lava ridges heading north.
Surroundings as capsule chains with real water levels: Kawaguchi (830 m, bent, narrow waist with a bridge), Yamanaka (980 m), Sai, Shoji, Motosu; Aokigahara forest; Fujiyoshida; the Misaka, Tenshi and Tanzawa ranges; Mount Ashitaka; Hakone; Suruga Bay coast and the Fuji River. A land-cover map (forest, fields, town, tea) computed in the same worker.
Far skyline beyond the world: a ring mesh 58-98 km out with the Southern Alps (W), Yatsugatake (NW), Chichibu (N), Tanzawa (E) and Izu (SE), open sea to the SW, seasonal snow. Past the 80 km edge the terrain shader fades to a low plain so nothing looks cut off.
3. Terrain rendering
Camera-centred geometry clipmap: 10 rings of 384 x 384 quads, 2 m cells doubling per ring, CDLOD-style morphing, inner-ring discard with a 2-cell overlap so cracks never open. 128-quad rings are too coarse: at 18 km they turn the notched summit into a hump.
When the camera is more than ~8.8 km from the summit, add a fixed 1024 x 1024 "hero" mesh (±7,600 m, 15 m spacing, with a skirt) for the cone so the silhouette is exact; sink the rings 6 m just outside it so the seam never shows.
Normals from central differences, fbm micro-displacement and detail normals near the camera. Clamp the camera above the ground everywhere.
Materials blended by height, slope, curvature and noise: scoria with rust bands, grey ash fans, treeline band, conifer and broadleaf forest (Aokigahara darkest), fields, towns (with night window lights), red-brown rock on steep walls. Skip the snow, forest and detail work for fragments that cannot see them.
Seasonal snow: winter cover to 1,500-2,000 m; late-spring streaks driven by curvature (gullies keep snow, ridges lose it); snow-free summer; autumn dusting on the top 300-500 m with autumn colours below. Subsurface tint, sparkle, sharper normals.
4. Light, sky and atmosphere
Hillaire-style atmosphere: transmittance LUT 256 x 64, multiple-scattering LUT 32 x 32, sky-view LUT 256 x 128 with absolute azimuth and two lights (sun and moon). Rayleigh, Mie, ozone and a low valley haze.
Ambient: SH9 projected from the sky-view LUT every time the sun moves.
Aerial perspective integrated per fragment through the same medium with adaptive steps (1 near, up to 8 far), so it works in mirror passes and on every built-in material.
Patch built-in three.js materials via onBeforeCompile for curvature, aerial perspective, terrain sun visibility and cloud shadow, so houses, trees, the train and the pagoda sit in the same light.
Terrain self-shadowing from a GPU sun-visibility map (2048 x 2048, a horizon march over the height textures with Earth curvature and a distance-growing penumbra), rebuilt in ~2 ms whenever the sun moves. It covers all 80 km and draws the mountain's own long shadow.
Object shadows: one shadow cascade following the camera (2048 at medium, 4096 at high); the terrain shader samples the same map.
Exposure computed from sun / moon elevation (deterministic, no adaptation history) and folded into light intensities so night keeps precision in half-float buffers. ACES filmic with toneMappingExposure = 0.6 to cancel three's /0.6.
Sky dome: sun disk with limb darkening, twilight, Earth shadow, Belt of Venus, sparse stars, a faint Milky Way, the moon, city glow.
5. Clouds
Raymarched from a 128^3 Perlin-Worley texture built in a worker from precomputed lattices (~1 s).
Density presets: cumulus; unkai sea of clouds at ~1,800 m; the kasa-gumo cap cloud as a hat-shaped dome with sharp tops, soft undersides, powder and silver lining plus two lens layers; an optional lenticular downwind; summit spindrift plumes.
Live mode: half resolution, 32 view steps, 3 light steps, temporal reprojection. Capture mode: full resolution, 84 view steps, 5 light steps, no history. Adaptive steps with empty-space skipping. A top-down cloud shadow map.
6. Water
Hand-written planar mirror per lake height (oblique near-plane clip, HalfFloat target with depth texture, scale 0.42 at medium and 0.75 at high or capture, MSAA 4 / 2), active only for lakes on screen. Hide petals, mist, birds and near trees in mirror passes.
Wind slider from mirror-still to breezy; Schlick fresnel, dark green-blue body, shoreline darkening, wet band.
Suruga Bay as a 240 x 110 km sea plane with real waves, sky reflection and sun glitter.
Two drifting mist sheets on Kawaguchi at dawn.
7. Vegetation and life
Instanced code-built trees: stacked noisy cones for conifers, smooth jittered icosahedron clusters for broadleaf and maples, cherries with falling petals. LOD tiers: full meshes within ~270 m, simplified to ~1 km, impostors from an atlas rendered at load to ~3.4 km, terrain colour beyond. Wind sway driven by scene time.
Black kites circling over the lakes; swan pedal boats and a sightseeing boat on Kawaguchi.
8. Human details
Chureito five-storey pagoda: stone base, five roofs with upturned corners, white walls, vermilion posts and brackets, railings, bronze finial with nine rings, a long stone stairway, cherry trees, a clear glade around it.
Fujiyoshida: ~7,000 instanced houses, a main street, roads, utility poles with sagging wires, a large vermilion torii aligned with the mountain, the Kawaguchi bridge, the 5th-station toll road and lake roads.
Yoshida trail zigzagging from 2,300 m with ~14 stone-walled huts set beside the switchbacks, a rim path, a shrine and torii on the rim, the summit station on Kengamine; glowing huts and a chain of moving headlamps at night.
A long white unbranded high-speed train with a blue stripe (16 cars) on a viaduct across the coastal plain, a girder bridge over the gravel bed of the Fuji River, and tea fields as curved hedge rows (instanced, capped ~110,000).
9. Post and performance
EffectComposer on a HalfFloat 4x MSAA target, very subtle per-shot bloom, a fade pass for dip-to-black cuts. No chromatic aberration, lens dirt or heavy vignette.
?q=low|med|high: low drops mirrors, MSAA and shadows and halves forest radii; high raises tree radii, mirror resolution and the shadow map. Target 60 fps at 1080p on an M-series Mac; the mirror and sea-of-clouds shots are the expensive ones.
10. Shots (~9 s each, slow eased moves, quick dip-to-black cuts)
Sakasa Fuji, Lake Kawaguchi: the upside-down mountain at dawn, autumn maples, mist. 18 Nov 06:40.
Chureito pagoda above Fujiyoshida, cherry blossoms, striped late-spring snow, descending. 12 Apr 08:20.
Red Fuji from the east, first light on the snow-free cone, kites. 28 Aug 05:24.
Kasa-gumo cap cloud from the WSW, Osawa-kuzure, spindrift, winter afternoon. 22 Jan 15:25.
Ouchi-in summit crater, drone over the rim, sea of clouds. 6 Aug 07:05.
Night climb: headlamps zigzagging up the Yoshida trail, huts, stars, Milky Way, town lights, fading to goraiko. 10 Aug 03:30-04:18.
High-speed train on the coastal plain, tea fields, the Hoei hump on the right skyline. 15 Jan 12:10.
Diamond Fuji from Lake Yamanaka, winter: solve the camera by back-projecting the summit along the real sun vector (sun elevation 0.5-18 degrees; at Yamanaka it lands near 10 degrees), kites.
Plus a free camera: drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, WASD fly, Q / E down / up, Shift for speed, never below ground.
11. HUD and URL
Minimal HUD: title "富士山 Mount Fuji 3,776 m", shot chips (keys 1-8), play / pause (space), date and time sliders (JST), season, cloud preset (clear, cumulus, cap cloud, sea of clouds), lake wind, fps; H hides it.
URL: ?shot=N&hold&hud=0&t=0&k=0.5&season=spring&time=05:40&q=low|med|high&capture&nocache&pr=1.
12. Tooling
window.__fuji.renderAt(t, shot, k, overrides) renders a deterministic frame: every animation (water, clouds, trees, birds, boats, train, headlamps, petals) runs on scene time, never the wall clock.
tools/record.py (Playwright headless Chromium with Metal ANGLE, 127.0.0.1 URLs, poll readiness with evaluate instead of wait_for_function): an EDIT list of the 8 shots totalling 54 s with 0.3 s dips, writing a silent 1080p60 H.264 X clip (video/mount-fuji.mp4, ~16 Mb/s) plus a CRF 11 master.

tools/shoot.py: stills to captures/, including named reference views (Kawaguchi, Fuji city, Gotemba).
13. Realism checklist
Kawaguchi silhouette (symmetric concave slopes, flat notched top, no Hoei hump); Hoei on the right from the south; Osawa-kuzure from the west; eroded, branched gullies; late-spring streaks; aerial perspective (hazy blue-grey base, crisp summit); shadows including the mountain's own; real sun positions and an aligned Diamond Fuji; correct reflections; no cracks, popping, shimmer or banding; life in every shot; clean console; frame-exact clip.
14. Process
PLAN.md first. Build the heightfield alone and check hillshades in node, then the clipmap, then sky and aerial perspective, then silhouette checks from Kawaguchi, Fuji city and Gotemba until the profile, notched top and Hoei hump read correctly. Then snow, clouds, lakes, vegetation, human details, shots, tooling and the clip, with a preview and screenshot after each stage. Ship README.md, PROMPT.md and an MIT LICENSE. Keep the git repo private until told otherwise.

mechanical-moth-329697.text:
在 Blender 中制作一支手绘质感的机械生物短片。雨夜的发明家工作台上，一只黄铜与晶体构成的机械飞蛾被青色电弧点亮，舒展肢体与翅翼，携带火花升空。画面兼具精巧的机械层次、温暖的桌面光和冷色魔法能量，第三段以「QWEN · IGNITE」片尾收束。  

完成场景、材质、绑定与动画，最终导出 3 段代表性视频、6 张高质量宣传图，并保存可编辑的 Blender 工程。  

## 场景与动作  
机械飞蛾长约成人掌心，拥有椭圆头部、较粗胸节、收细的分节腹部和六条细长机械足。金色与黄铜外骨骼有清楚的铰链、嵌件和磨损边缘；头部两侧是青绿色发光晶体眼，胸部是一枚可看见内部亮点的晶体核心。头顶两根长触角向外弯曲，触角两侧密排梳齿般的细分支。  

两对翅翼从胸部左右连接，黄铜细框分出昆虫翅脉，框内镶有半透明青绿、暖琥珀和淡玫瑰色晶体薄片。翅根、前后翅和腹部关节分别运动，收翼时薄片有层叠厚度，展翼时轮廓完整。脚掌落在桌面上时有明确支点，抬胸会带动前足伸直，起飞前后足有蹬离动作。  

场景是一张有使用痕迹的木质工作台，中央铺一张暖黄色大纸张，纸边轻微卷起，表面有淡淡构造线。边缘摆放细金属工具、导线线圈、零件盘和一盏低亮度工作灯，后方的大窗占据主要背景，窗玻璃有斜向雨痕，窗外是失焦的深青夜城与零星暖窗灯。  

开场飞蛾低伏、核心暗淡。细电弧沿触角和翅脉跳动，能量集中到胸腔，核心由暗青变为明亮蓝绿；身体随脉冲短促一震，晶体眼依次亮起。火花以白芯、青色边缘的尖锐图形与少量暖金粒子表现，先爆发后迅速衰减，保留黄铜结构的可读性。  

采用绘画式表面：木面、纸张、金属和远景都有有方向的笔触与设计过的阴影色块。机械动作带清楚的预备、停顿和弹性回落，摄像机平稳连续；角色姿态可按每两帧一拍设计，电弧和火花具有逐拍变化的图形感。第三段最后使用深青背景、精致暖金字形的「QWEN · IGNITE」，细小青紫光粒从字边掠过，约 1.5 秒稳定可读。  

## 环境规模、背景层次与精细度  
工作台是有使用痕迹、值得细看的完整发明家空间。前景以卷边纸张、工具边缘和零件引导视线，中景是飞蛾、线圈、零件盘和台灯，后景以窗框、雨痕、窗外高低错落的夜城轮廓和疏密变化的暖窗灯形成纵深。金属、纸张、木材和湿玻璃分别具有细腻的表面与反光，飞蛾升空时窗外灯群和室内陈设仍能交代空间尺度。片尾前的环境镜头保持绘画般丰富的冷暖色块与清楚的主体层级。

  ## 画面风格与光照  
使用风格化材质与分层合成统一笔触、晶体透光和图形化特效。工作台为暖琥珀色，窗外为深青蓝，晶体核心为青绿；景深将主体与雨夜背景分开，光晕集中在晶体和电弧周围。渲染可采用 Eevee 或 Cycles，以稳定的手绘质感和清晰形体为准。  

## 三段代表性视频  
每段单独成片，目标时长 **6 秒、24 fps、144 帧**，具有完整的进入、主体动作与收束。以下时间为各段内时间，动作节拍可作自然调整。三段中重复出现的主体与环境保持造型、尺度和材质一致。

time-flashlight-920447.text:
请设计并实现一个令人过目不忘的交互式网页作品：

《时间不是进度条，是一把手电筒》
TIME IS A FLASHLIGHT
你是一位交互艺术家、创意前端工程师和电影美术指导。请直接交付可以运行的完整作品，不要只给方案、示意图或代码片段。

【核心体验】

浏览器里是一座被封存在玻璃展柜中的微缩城市。

展柜之外漆黑安静，桌面上有磨损的黄铜铭牌、年代刻度和一只机械调节旋钮。城市内部有钟楼、电车轨道、车站、街巷、树木，以及几栋可以辨认的建筑。

用户移动鼠标，相当于移动一束“时间手电筒”。

光束之外，是荒废已久的城市。
光束之内，是用户选择的年代。

同一座钟楼，可以一半是锈蚀废墟，另一半仍灯火通明；同一条街道，可以一侧长满植物，另一侧有电车经过。年代之间必须空间对齐，不能通过切换两张背景图假装实现。
第一眼让人想停下来，第一次移动鼠标就让人理解玩法，继续探索则不断发现细节。

【视觉方向】

整体像一件真实存在的博物馆互动装置，具有微缩模型摄影的质感。

采用等距或轻透视俯视构图，让建筑、街道与时间切面容易辨认。城市占据主要画面，界面控件像装置上的实体零件。

视觉元素：

深炭黑环境、暖象牙白文字、氧化铜、少量琥珀色灯光。

建筑有明确体积、遮挡关系、接触阴影和细小窗户。
玻璃边缘有克制的反光，不能盖住主体。
废墟有断裂结构、植被侵入、熄灭的路灯。
繁华时代有暖窗、电车、少量移动人影。
尚未建成的时代呈现测绘线、地基、建筑轮廓和手写标注。
不要常规首页、卡片网格、后台布局、紫色渐变、满屏霓虹，也不要用大量文字解释创意。字体、留白、按钮和细节应与这件装置属于同一个世界。
【必须实现的交互】

时间光束
鼠标移动控制光束位置，边缘具有柔和但清晰的年代过渡。光束应揭示另一个年代真实存在的建筑和动态内容，不只是提亮、调色或模糊。

鼠标滚轮调整光束半径；提供可见的替代控件。光束内的微小尘埃和边缘折射可以增加质感，但不能影响辨认。

机械年代旋钮
用户拖动旋钮，在三个年代之间连续调整：
1920：尚未建成的城市，蓝图、地基和施工结构。

1980：繁华的城市，电车、亮灯的车站和街道。

2080：被遗忘的城市，植物覆盖、结构残缺。
年代变化必须体现在场景本身。允许用阶段插值与交叉过渡实现，但建筑位置、道路和地标必须保持一致。
旋钮要有指针、刻度、拖动反馈及键盘操作。数字读数与画面状态实时同步。
固定时间窗口
点击“钉住这一刻”，将当前光束保存为一个固定时间窗口，保留它自己的年代和半径。
最多保留三个窗口。用户可以移动、关闭这些窗口，并继续移动手中的光束。

每个窗口必须保持独立状态。窗口重叠时使用明确且稳定的显示优先级，不要闪烁或随机变化。

让用户能够同时看到：蓝图中的钟楼、繁华时代的车站、废墟中的街区。

城市里的小秘密
设计三个可以通过探索发现的细节，例如：
废墟车站的长椅，在过去坐着一个等车的人。

倒塌的钟楼，在过去会准点摆动钟摆。

一棵占据街道的大树，在早期只是路边的一株树苗。

发现时仅出现一句克制的短文案，避免弹窗打断体验。命中检测必须对应用户实际看到的年代与位置，不能点击空白处也触发。

自动演示
提供“让时间自己走一会儿”按钮，启动约 20 秒的编排演示：光束移动、年代变化、展示不同地标，最后回到可操作状态。
用户随时操作都应立即接管，不能与演示争抢控制权。
【开场与细节】
打开后立即看到完成度高的城市，不要用加载动画拖延。
开场用一次短暂的光束掠过，自然展示“同一建筑的两个年代”，随后显示一句提示：

“移动光，看看这里曾经是什么样子。”

界面文案使用中文，英文仅作少量辅助标识。
加入可关闭的环境音，通过用户首次交互后启动；可以用 Web Audio 程序化生成轻微机械声、电车铃声和空间氛围，不依赖外部音频文件。

【技术要求】

交付一个完整、自包含的 HTML 文件，包含全部 CSS 和 JavaScript。

场景素材用代码生成，不依赖外部图片、视频、模型或付费资源。

可选择 Canvas、SVG、WebGL 或组合方案，以最终效果和交互稳定性为准。

城市各年代共享同一套空间坐标与地标数据。

不能把整个作品做成预渲染视频，也不能用静态插画代替核心交互。

正确处理高分屏、窗口缩放、指针离开、拖动取消和坐标换算。

桌面端优先，同时支持手机触摸移动光束，以及通过控件调节半径与年代。

限制粒子与绘制成本，避免不断累积动画循环和事件监听。
尊重 prefers-reduced-motion，并提供暂停动态效果的入口。
所有可见按钮必须真实可用。
【验收标准】
我会亲自测试以下行为：
移动光束，检查同一栋建筑是否准确对齐。
改变年代，检查城市内容是否真实变化。
固定三个不同年代的窗口，检查它们是否保留独立状态。
移动并关闭窗口，检查是否出现残影或错误遮挡。
在自动演示中主动拖动旋钮，检查能否立即接管。
缩放窗口，检查光束和交互热点是否仍然准确。
请把主要精力放在城市的视觉完成度、时间切面的惊奇感和交互的完整性上。宁可精心完成一个街区，也不要堆砌一大片简陋方块。
最终交付的是一件可以亲手探索的互动艺术作品。现在直接实现。

marginalia-atlas-1xtymff.text:
Act as an elite creative director, award-winning frontend engineer, interaction designer, and creative technologist. Build an extraordinary, production-quality website that feels like an interactive piece of digital art rather than a traditional website. Aim for Awwwards Site of the Day / Site of the Year quality.

### 1. Art direction
Create a distinctive visual universe combining:
- An artist's sketchbook, hand-drawn notebook, and experimental digital canvas.
- Editorial typography, museum-quality layouts, handmade illustrations, doodles, pencil sketches, scribbles, ink strokes, paper textures, marginal annotations, stamps, and sticky notes.
- A living artistic painting that evolves as visitors explore.
- Beautiful, unconventional compositions with asymmetrical grids, overlapping layers, and intentional whitespace.
- A cohesive visual identity that feels handcrafted, premium, playful, cinematic, and original.

Avoid generic SaaS layouts, predictable cards, repetitive sections, default gradients, and basic fade-in animations.

### 2. Cinematic scroll-driven storytelling
Scrolling must feel like traveling through a continuous artwork, not moving down a stack of sections.

Implement a seamless zoom-in → reveal → zoom-out → pan → zoom-in journey:
- Begin with a massive illustrated canvas or artistic painting containing multiple worlds, drawings, and hidden details.
- As the user scrolls, smoothly zoom into one small object inside the painting.
- That object expands into an entirely new interactive section.
- As scrolling continues, pull the camera backward, revealing that the entire section is part of another illustration.
- Pan or rotate across the larger canvas and zoom into the next visual element.
- Repeat with varied compositions and transitions, creating a continuous, nested-world experience.
- Use depth, parallax, camera transforms, perspective changes, masking, morphing, and seamless scene transitions.
- Reverse transitions naturally when scrolling upward.

Animations must be synchronized to scroll progress, responsive to scrolling velocity, and polished enough to feel cinematic.

### 3. Interactive notebook and realistic paper physics
Build an interactive sketchbook experience with:
- Notebook pages that flip, fold, curl, and cast realistic shadows.
- Live paper-tearing interactions: visitors can grab a perforated edge and physically drag to tear off a page or note.
- Real-time tear progression, deformation, irregular ripped edges, and believable paper movement.
- Loose paper scraps that fall, float, or react to cursor movement.
- Handwritten annotations that animate as though an invisible artist is drawing them.
- Doodles that come alive on hover, sketches that transform into interactive components, and sticky notes that can be dragged and rearranged.
- Realistic page transitions, texture layering, and subtle paper sounds with optional audio controls.

Use SVG paths, masks, clipping, physics simulations, and GPU-accelerated animations where appropriate. Make the tearing genuinely interactive, not a prerecorded visual effect.

### 4. Interactive flow-diagram module
Integrate an advanced interactive flowchart or mind-map experience using React Flow (`@xyflow/react`) or an equivalent system.

Include draggable nodes, animated connections, smooth zoom/pan, expandable sections, dynamic node creation, editable relationships, custom-drawn nodes, and live updates.

Make the flow diagram visually compatible with the sketchbook theme: hand-drawn arrows, animated ink connections, organic node shapes, and flowing particles. It must be functional rather than decorative.

### 5. Signature interactions and creative experiments
Introduce several memorable experiences:
- Morphing SVG illustrations and animated line art.
- Cursor-reactive elements, magnetic buttons, custom pointer effects, and hover distortions.
- Text that draws itself, rearranges, or reveals hidden illustrations.
- Interactive 2D/3D objects embedded within illustrations.
- Scroll-controlled horizontal galleries, pinned scenes, and experimental transitions.
- Interactive canvases where visitors can draw or manipulate elements.
- Physics-based objects, paper scraps, ink particles, and interactive typography.
- Micro-interactions that communicate meaning rather than adding random visual noise.
- Clever easter eggs and delightful hidden details.

Design at least three truly original signature moments that make the experience memorable.

### 6. Recommended technology
Choose the best architecture for the experience, using modern production-ready tools where appropriate:

- Next.js, React, TypeScript.
- GSAP and ScrollTrigger for cinematic scroll timelines, pinning, scrubbing, and zoom transitions.
- Lenis for smooth, controlled scrolling.
- Motion for React for component animations and layout transitions.
- Three.js / React Three Fiber / WebGL where actual 3D depth improves the experience.
- React Flow for interactive node-based diagrams.
- SVG, Canvas, CSS masks, clip-path, and shaders for drawing, paper effects, and experimental visuals.
- Matter.js or appropriate physics tools for physical interactions.

Use animation libraries selectively. Prioritize coherent art direction, performance, and excellent interaction design over unnecessary dependencies.

### 7. Use award-winning GitHub design skills
Research and apply relevant Awwwards-inspired frontend agent skills, including `juliobsz/skills` (/awwwards), `Ga14ctic/awwwards-skill`, and high-quality creative frontend and motion-design references.

Follow a professional creative-development process: concept exploration, visual identity, composition, interaction architecture, implementation, polish, browser testing, and refinement.

Do not copy an existing award-winning website. Create an original visual concept with comparable craftsmanship.

### 8. Performance and accessibility
- Smooth animations targeting 60 FPS on capable devices.
- Responsive experiences across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
- Graceful degradation for devices without powerful GPUs.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences.
- Lazy-load heavy scenes and assets.
- Use semantic HTML, accessible controls, and keyboard navigation.
- Maintain correct scroll behavior without jitter, broken pinned sections, or layout shifts.
- Ensure every visible interactive control actually works.

### 9. Execution requirements
First establish a distinctive creative concept and cohesive design system. Then implement the complete website, including real assets, interactions, component states, and animations.

Do not stop after a mockup, wireframe, static landing page, or initial hero section.

Build the actual application, run it, test the scroll journey and interactions in a browser, capture screenshots, identify weak visual areas, and refine until it feels like a cohesive, exceptional interactive artwork.

**Ultimate objective:** The visitor should feel as if they are exploring a magical, living sketchbook and traveling inside an evolving painting, with seamless zoom transitions that turn illustrations into entire functional web experiences. Every interaction should feel intentional, artistic, technically impressive, and unforgettable.

# Three.js Procedural Low-Poly Horse Benchmark

## Objective

Create a high-quality, fully modelled and animated low-poly horse using Three.js use CDN. The result should resemble a professionally constructed low-poly game asset, not a simple collection of geometric primitives.

Build the horse procedurally in code. Do not use external 3D models, GLTF/GLB files, downloaded assets, image planes or pre-made character models.

Prioritise modelling quality, convincing anatomy, deliberate geometry and polished animation. Do not sacrifice the quality of the horse to produce a more elaborate interface.

## Reference images

Three reference images are supplied:

- **horse-1.jpg — Overall appearance / anatomy:** Primary guide for proportions, silhouette, muscle volumes and presentation. Tan/brown body, black mane/tail, dark lower legs. Do not copy its smooth shading — final must be flat-shaded low-poly.
- **horse-3.jpg — Polygon style / density target:** Primary guide for polygon density, geometry distribution, facet size and flat-shaded appearance. This is the 2500-3500 triangle reference. Study facet distribution: higher density on head, shoulders, hips and joints, larger facets on barrel and neck.
- **horse-2.jpg — Colour/facet style only:** Reference for flat facets and palette only. Do NOT copy its density — it is far below the 2500-3500 budget and too coarse for the required anatomy.

Treat these images as visual requirements rather than loose inspiration. Where they conflict, precedence is horse-1.jpg for form/proportions, horse-3.jpg for density/distribution.

## 1. Modelling and geometry

Create a complete horse with convincing equine anatomy and recognisable proportions. It should look like a carefully constructed 3D asset rather than a collection of basic geometric shapes.

Use sufficient geometry to communicate anatomical form while retaining a clearly visible low-poly aesthetic. The horse body including mane, tail, ears and hooves (excluding ground/scene/UI) should be made up of between 2500 and 3500 polygons/triangles total, counted as triangles via `renderer.info.render.triangles` with ground/scene hidden. Distribute polygons where they contribute to the silhouette, anatomy and visible form. Avoid both extremely coarse geometry and unnecessarily dense, smooth geometry.

Build from sculpted cross-section loops with distinct volumes for chest, barrel, belly and hindquarters — not boxes, capsules, cylinders or spheres. Maintain horse proportions (use shoulder-to-hip = 1 unit: back roughly level, chest deep, hindquarters rounded, neck curved ~40-50° from horizontal, head length ~1/4 body length, legs long with clearly offset knee/hock heights fore vs hind). Spend density on head/jaw/muzzle, shoulder/hip transitions and leg joints; keep barrel and mid-neck facets larger as in horse-3.jpg. Silhouette must read as horse from front, side, rear and three-quarter views in both neutral pose and mid-gallop.

Include:

- **Head:** Defined forehead, cheeks, jaw, muzzle and nostrils.
- **Eyes:** Visible, correctly positioned eyes with suitable geometry and materials.
- **Ears:** Two distinct, pointed ears.
- **Neck:** Curved, muscular neck with a clear transition into the shoulders and chest.
- **Torso:** Defined chest, barrel, back, abdomen and hindquarters.
- **Legs:** Four separately modelled, articulated legs with plausible equine proportions and visible joints.
- **Hooves:** Distinct, properly shaped hooves with clear geometry.
- **Mane:** Volumetric, polygonal mane with layered strands or clumps rather than a flat strip.
- **Tail:** Volumetric polygonal tail with a recognisable shape.

Pay particular attention to the horse's silhouette. Its proportions and shape should remain convincing from the front, side, rear and three-quarter views.

Avoid cylindrical legs with no anatomical shaping, spherical joints, obvious primitive placeholders, a featureless capsule-shaped torso, a block-like head or neck, flat details that only work from one camera angle, and geometry so coarse that important anatomical forms disappear.

## 2. Low-poly visual style

Use an intentional low-poly aesthetic:

- Flat-shaded triangular and polygonal surfaces.
- Clearly visible facets and deliberate changes in surface direction.
- Enough polygons to represent the anatomy and silhouette convincingly.
- Natural horse colours, with restrained variation between selected faces.
- A coherent material palette and consistent visual style.

The model should look deliberately low-poly, not unfinished or under-modelled. Do not use smooth shading to hide inadequate geometry.

## 3. Locomotion and animation

Implement a complete horse locomotion system with the following animation states.

Research https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Horse_in_Motion text and images to learn how a horse moves naturally, and use it to inform gait timing, leg sequencing, foot placement, and body movement.

### Idle
- Natural standing pose.
- Subtle breathing and body movement.
- Small head and neck movements.
- Occasional ear movement.
- Subtle tail movement.

### Walk
- Convincing four-beat walking gait.
- Natural foot placement and weight transfer.
- Appropriate movement through the shoulders, hips, torso, neck and head.

### Trot
- Recognisable diagonal leg pairing.
- Increased body movement.
- Appropriate suspension and foot placement.

### Canter
- Recognisable three-beat gait.
- Coordinated leg movement.
- Visible suspension and natural body movement.

### Gallop
- Fast, dynamic running motion.
- Convincing galloping leg sequence.
- Extended and gathered leg positions.
- Pronounced suspension phase.
- Coordinated movement through the spine, torso, shoulders, hips, neck and head.
- It can try to use `motion-capture/index.html` to help with movement of the legs: it contains a side-view transverse gallop mocap reference with skeleton joint positions, stance/swing phases, footfall order/timings (LH/RH/LF/RF), and two-bone IK for knees/hocks. Use it as a guide for gallop leg phasing, lift/fold, and hoof placement.

### Rig and articulation

- Hierarchy: `root > spine > [chest > neckBase > neckMid > head > (jaw, 2 ears)] + [4x shoulder/hip > knee/hock > fetlock > hoof]`, plus separate mane/tail chains.
- Place pivots at anatomical joints, not mesh centres. Primary rotation on one hinge axis per joint plus small twist only.
- Animate in place (no root travel); stance feet must plant without visible sliding.
- Spine/neck/head must counter-move per gait to preserve balance, not stay rigid.

### Animation quality

- Animate all four legs independently.
- Use appropriate articulation at the shoulders, hips, knees, hocks, fetlocks and hooves.
- Maintain anatomically plausible limb positions throughout each gait.
- Include believable weight distribution and centre-of-mass movement.
- Animate the spine, torso, neck and head to complement each gait.
- Add secondary movement to the mane, tail and ears.
- Avoid mechanical, robotic or synchronised movement that does not resemble a horse.

### Transitions and playback

- Provide smooth transitions between all animation states.
- Allow the horse to progress from walking through trotting and cantering into a gallop, and decelerate back to walking or idle.
- Blend transitions naturally, without sudden limb-position changes or animation discontinuities.
- Make animation speed adjustable.
- Use delta time for frame-rate-independent animation.
- Ensure each gait loops seamlessly.

## 4. Interactive camera controls

Implement interactive camera controls so the horse can be inspected from any angle:

- **Orbit:** Rotate the camera around the horse using mouse drag.
- **Pan:** Move the camera target horizontally and vertically.
- **Zoom:** Zoom in and out using the mouse wheel.
- **Touch support:** Provide equivalent gestures on touch devices where practical.
- Set sensible minimum and maximum zoom distances.
- Prevent the camera from moving below the ground plane.
- Keep the horse as the camera's focal point.
- Provide a reset-camera button.
- Keep the horse correctly framed when the viewport is resized.

Use `THREE.OrbitControls` where appropriate.

## 5. Animation control panel

Provide a compact interface for testing the model:

- Animation selector: Idle, Walk, Trot, Canter and Gallop.
- Play/pause control.
- Animation speed slider.
- Smooth transitions when switching animation states.
- Reset animation button.
- Reset camera button.

The controls must be functional, clearly labelled and visually unobtrusive. The horse should remain the main focus.

## 6. Scene and presentation

Present the horse in a professional 3D showcase environment:

- Three-quarter default camera angle.
- Orthographic or perspective camera with appropriate framing.
- Ground plane with convincing contact shadows.
- Professional lighting with soft shadows.
- Neutral background that makes the horse stand out.
- Ensure the entire horse is visible in the initial view.

The scene should make the geometry easy to inspect without distracting from the model.

## 7. Technical requirements

- Use Three.js.
- Generate all horse geometry programmatically.
- Do not use external model assets or substitute missing details with primitive placeholders.
- Use `BufferGeometry` where appropriate.
- Use hierarchical groups for articulated body parts.
- Organise modelling, materials, scene setup and animation into reusable functions or modules.
- Use flat-shaded materials.
- Use delta time for animation updates.
- Handle window resizing correctly.
- Ensure camera controls and animation controls work together.
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
- Ensure the application runs without errors.

## 8. Quality expectations and priorities

The final result should resemble a professionally modelled low-poly game asset, with deliberate geometry, convincing anatomy, a detailed silhouette and polished animation.

The horse must maintain convincing anatomical proportions and geometry throughout every animation state. Pay particular attention to the legs, shoulders, hips and neck during the gallop. The model must remain visually convincing when inspected closely from any camera angle.

Prioritise work in this order:

1. High-quality modelling and anatomical accuracy.
2. Convincing locomotion across all five animation states.
3. Geometry and shading that achieve the supplied low-poly references.
4. Interactive camera and animation controls.
5. Scene presentation and code organisation.

Meeting the 2500-3500 triangle budget is required, but count alone does not pass — the result is judged by the actual 3D asset and its animation, not merely by an attractive initial screenshot or UI completion.

Acceptance: provide wireframe toggle and live triangle-count readout (ground/scene excluded) to prove budget; verify silhouette in front/side/rear/three-quarter views and in neutral pose plus mid-gallop extension/gather.

## 9. Phase 2 — Scenery (after Phase 1 complete)

Only start once §§1-8 are complete and accepted. Do not regress horse modelling, rig, gaits, or the 2500-3500 triangle horse budget to build scenery.

Replace/extend the neutral showcase in §6 with a next-level quality low-poly trail environment. Scenery objects must be in the same flat-shaded style as the horse but richer — no skimping, MORE polygons where it reads. Fully formed silhouettes from all camera angles.

**Style:** faceted geometry with flat shading throughout — visible triangles, each a single solid colour, no texture maps, no smooth normals. Light changes shade facet to facet for crystal look. Simple chunky shapes that read at a glance. Warm soft storybook mood, not realism.

**Composition (layered depth):** foreground dirt track in tan/ochre large angular patches in slightly different tones, with grass-blade tufts, pebbles and stemmed flowers; midground wooden post-and-rail fence parallel to default view with grassy meadow behind dotted with trees, rocks and tufts; background rolling hills in lighter olive greens, then grey-brown mountains with pale snow/rock caps fading into hazy lavender-grey sky. Default camera low, roughly eye level, moderate FOV, horizon fairly high so trees loom.

**Palette:** greens carry the scene from dark pine to bright yellow-green meadow/canopies; warm earth tan/caramel dirt and reddish-brown wood; cool muted greys/mauves for mountains, clouds and sky. Moderate saturation, warm late-afternoon values overall.

**Lighting and atmosphere:** one directional sun from upper left/front with soft-edged ground shadows; hemisphere/ambient fill so shadow sides stay readable; atmospheric perspective with distant hills/mountains lighter, bluer/greyer, fog-tinted toward sky colour. Clouds as flattened lumpy faceted masses in white/grey.

**Variation and touches:** random variation in tree height, rotation, scale and tint; low-poly dust puffs at hooves; ground as large angular patches with subtle colour variation, never a flat plane.

Include, all procedural `BufferGeometry`, flat-shaded, no external assets:

- **Wooden fence:** one side of trail only, capped posts with slight lean/rotation jitter plus 2-3 rails with joints/breaks, per-piece brown variation.
